Description: The message shown to Java Edition players in the server list. Use § for colour codes. Line breaks are not supported.
The message shown to Bedrock Edition players in the server list.
Sets the name of the level (world) folder to load, or create if it does not exist.
Sets the seed used to generate a new world. Leave empty for a random seed. Only applies when the world is first created.
Sets the maximum number of players allowed on the server at one time. Applied separately to Java and Bedrock Edition.
Whether Java Edition clients can connect.
Whether Bedrock Edition clients can connect.
Whether to show a server icon in the server list. Pumpkin's default icon is used if the file below is missing.
Path to a 64x64 PNG server icon, relative to the server folder.
Whether the server accepts players transferred from other servers.
Sets the game mode for new players.
If set, players are switched to the default game mode every time they join.
Sets the difficulty level of the world.
If set, players cannot respawn after dying.
Sets the permission level for players who are not operators.
The permission level assigned by the /op command.
Non-operators cannot place or break blocks within this many blocks of the world spawn. Set to 0 to disable.
Whether players can damage each other.
Whether players in Creative mode are protected from PVP.
Whether attacks apply knockback.
Whether players swing their hand when attacking.
Whether to show the red hurt animation and FOV bobbing when hit.
Enable April Fools features.
Sets the maximum view distance for players. Higher values have a performance impact.
Sets the distance around each player in which the world is ticked. Higher values have a performance impact.
Whether the Nether dimension is enabled.
Whether the End dimension is enabled.
Default uses vanilla lighting. Full lights everything (no shadows). Dark makes everything completely dark.
The storage format for world chunks. Anvil is the vanilla format and is compatible with other servers and tools. WARNING: changing this for an existing world will make it fail to load.
Anvil only. Whether to write chunk data directly into region files.
The server's target tick rate. Vanilla is 20.
How often the world is saved, in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second). 0 disables autosave.
Anvil only. Compression algorithm for stored chunks.
Anvil only. Compression level for stored chunks.
Whether network packets to Java Edition clients are compressed.
Packets smaller than this are not compressed.
1 favours speed, 9 favours smaller packets.
Whether network packets to Bedrock Edition clients are compressed.
Packets smaller than this are not compressed.
1 favours speed, 9 favours smaller packets.
Whether Bedrock Edition clients may cache chunk data to reduce bandwidth.
Kick clients that send packets faster than the limit below. Applies to Java and Bedrock Edition.
Maximum packets per second allowed from each client. 0 disables the limit.
Number of packets a client may send in a short burst above the rate limit.
Message shown to clients kicked by the packet limiter.
Whether player data is saved to disk.
How often player data is saved.
Whether player advancements are saved and loaded.
Whether to send recipe book data to players. Disabling this can significantly improve login performance.
Enables support for proxies. Also enable the specific proxy type below.
Whether Velocity proxy support is enabled.
The forwarding secret configured in Velocity.
Whether BungeeCord proxy support is enabled.
Optional BungeeGuard token. When set, connections without a matching token are rejected, which also blocks players bypassing the proxy.
Whether Vine proxy support is enabled.
The Ed25519 public key of the Vine proxy (64 hex characters).
Optional shared secret. If set and the public key is empty, the public key is derived from it.
Whether to answer Query protocol requests on the Java Edition port (UDP).
Whether the RCON remote console is enabled. RCON will not start without a password.
The password used for RCON authentication.
The maximum number of simultaneous RCON connections. 0 = unlimited.
Advertise the server to Java Edition clients on the local network. Only useful when players are on the same network as the server.
One-line message shown to LAN clients. Leave empty to use the server MOTD.
The local UDP port used to send LAN broadcasts. 0 = random port (default). If LAN broadcast does not work, set a static port here and allocate it in AMP.
Public IP address advertised to Bedrock clients when the server is behind NAT. Must be an IP address, not a hostname. Leave empty to detect it automatically.
If set, Java Edition players must have a valid Minecraft account. Requires Enable Encryption.
Whether Java Edition packet encryption is enabled. Must stay enabled while Online Mode is on, or the server will not start.
Whether Java Edition players are verified with Mojang's session servers.
If set, Bedrock Edition players must be signed in to Xbox Live.
Whether Bedrock Edition players are verified with Xbox Live.
Text added to the start of Bedrock Edition player names, so they cannot clash with Java Edition names. Leave empty for no prefix.
Replace spaces in Bedrock Edition player names with underscores, so they can be used in commands.
If set, only players on the whitelist can join.
Kick online players who are not on the whitelist when it is reloaded.
Whether to hide players' IP addresses in the logs.
Whether to block players connecting through a VPN or proxy.
Timeout when connecting to the authentication server.
Timeout when reading from the authentication server.
Allow players flagged by Mojang (forced name change or banned skin) to join.
Whether player skins, capes and elytras are loaded from Mojang.
Send anonymous usage heartbeats to the Pumpkin project (pumpkinmc.org).
Show this server in the public Pumpkin community directory. Requires Enable Telemetry.
Whether to send a resource pack to Java Edition clients.
The direct download URL of the resource pack.
The SHA1 hash (40 characters) of the resource pack.
The message shown to players when asked to download the pack. Leave empty for none.
Whether players must accept the resource pack to join.
Whether to send resource packs to Bedrock Edition clients.
Whether players must accept the resource packs to join.
Whether to use player skins.
Whether to use player capes.
Whether to use player elytra textures.
The log verbosity level.
Name of the log file inside the logs folder. Leave empty to disable file logging.
Whether commands run by players are logged to the console.
Whether console and RCON command output is shown to online operators.
Whether successful RCON logins are logged.
Whether failed RCON logins are logged.
Whether commands run over RCON are logged.
Whether RCON disconnects are logged.
Whether to show server links in the Java Edition pause menu.
URL for the bug report link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the support link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the status link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the feedback link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the community link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the website link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the forums link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the news link. Leave empty to hide it.
URL for the announcements link. Leave empty to hide it.
Format for chat messages. {DISPLAYNAME} and {MESSAGE} are replaced. Does not apply when Allow Chat Reports is enabled.
Use signed chat so players can report messages to Mojang. Requires Online Mode, or the server will not start.
Kick players who send chat messages or commands too quickly.
Whether operators are exempt from anti-spam.
Players are kicked when their spam counter reaches this value. Vanilla is 200.
Amount added to the spam counter for each message or command. Vanilla is 20.
Amount removed from the spam counter every tick. Vanilla is 1.
Whether plugins in the plugins folder are loaded.
Watch the plugins folder and reload plugins automatically when they change.
Ask in the console before granting new permissions requested by a plugin. Answer in the AMP console.
Whether unsigned WASM plugins can be loaded.
Whether WASM plugin signatures are verified before loading.
Whether plugins can read the server's environment variables.
Restrict plugin network access to localhost.
Which Pumpkin build to install. Stable is the latest release. Canary is the newest development build and may change settings without notice. Run an update after changing this.
